title: Keeping the melody recognizable
summary: He always kept some semblance of the melody so listeners could identify the tune.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: -- you did it on the spot?

Well, not too much on the spot, but most of the others I had planned. And another thing, in playing a tune I always kept the idea that there should always be some semblance of the melody, and never get too far away so they couldn't can -- so that the public couldn't tell what you were playing. And so, although you may play around the melody for a while, but come back to it so that they could identify it and say oh that's so and so.
And because if you did -- if you played around on every tune, what tune would it be, see. The melody has to come through enough so you can identify one tune from another.
And I used that system all the time.
